title: Mara and the Extraction
premise: Rafael Amberdale, a crash investigator whose wife and daughter died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent three years hiding in a safe house under a polished lie: that the crash was mechanical failure and he saw nothing. But when the safe house is listed for sale online — with interior photos revealing his evidence wall — he realizes someone inside the investigation sold him out. Racing across borders with a go-bag of black-box fragments, he is hunted by an assassin named Mara Voss, who begins to question her employers as she closes in. To survive, Rafael must smuggle the truth past three complicit governments before the border checkpoint shift change gives his hunters a clean window to kill him; in the end, Mara chooses love against duty, letting him live and testifying alongside him, while the corrupt aviation director falls.
about_author: Freya Marchetti is a former airline safety analyst turned novelist who writes thrillers from a farmhouse in the Dolomites. Her work draws on a decade spent reading accident reports, where she learned that every disaster has two stories: the one published, and the one buried.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He wakes at 3 a.m., checks the door bolts, and recites his cover story like a prayer before visiting the memorial garden where row twelve's names are carved. Emotional beat: grief calcified into routine, and the first crack — a realtor's flyer for his own house, photos showing his evidence wall.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He traces the listing to a boutique agency and finds the photographer's metadata points to a government-issued camera. Someone authorized this. He packs the go-bag, burns nothing yet, and photographs the wall himself. Emotional beat: cold panic hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Black Box Fragments
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn what's in the bag: cockpit voice recorder chips he stole from the wreckage site, proving the flight was downed by a jammed transponder order, not weather. Emotional beat: the lie he tells himself — that he kept them for closure — collapses into truth: he kept them as leverage.

chapters.title: Mara Voss, Contractor
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She receives the contract: retrieve the fragments, leave no witnesses. She studies Rafael's file and notices the same anomaly she was hired to ignore three years ago. Emotional beat: professional detachment with a hairline fracture already running through it.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Posing as a buyer, she tours the safe house and finds Rafael gone but not sloppy — a tripwire on the shed, a decoy laptop still warm. Emotional beat: grudging respect; the prey is better than the file promised.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Nine
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At a rural border crossing he talks his way past a bored guard using his old investigator credentials — credentials that should have been revoked hours ago. Someone wants him mobile, trackable. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening; the trap has walls he can't see.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating brief POVs of a transport minister, an intelligence deputy, and an aviation director, each covering their piece of the downing. Emotional beat: banality of corruption — men deleting emails over coffee while ordering a man's death.

chapters.title: The Hotel With Two Exits
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In a border city he meets Lena Okonjo, a journalist who once investigated the crash and was ruined for it. She offers archives; he offers the chips. Emotional beat: first belonging since row twelve — terrifying because it makes him targetable.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She corners Rafael in a parking garage; instead of killing him she asks one question about the transponder logs. He answers honestly. She lets him walk, reporting a missed shot. Emotional beat: duty bending under doubt.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her handler replaces her with a second team and orders her to clean up 'the asset problem' — meaning herself. She realizes she was always disposable. Emotional beat: the assassin discovering she is also prey.

chapters.title: Lena's Archive
chapters.summary: Rafael and Lena's shared POV. The archive confirms a maintenance order forged six hours before takeoff, signed by the aviation director. Emotional beat: hope — dangerous, intoxicating hope — and the growing pull between Rafael and Lena.

chapters.title: The Second Team
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The replacement assassins hit the hotel; Lena is wounded covering their escape through the kitchen. Rafael uses investigator tradecraft — fire exits, service elevators, sightlines — to get them out. Emotional beat: guilt and fury fused into resolve.

chapters.title: An Assassin's Mercy
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She intercepts the wounded pair, disarms the second team's scout instead, and gives Rafael a burner phone with the checkpoint rotation schedule. 'I'm not saving you,' she lies. Emotional beat: love against duty, unnamed but undeniable.

chapters.title: What Mara Knows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, flashback. Three years ago she ran security for the same director and was ordered to stand down the night of the flight. She has carried it like shrapnel ever since. Emotional beat: confession to herself; the fracture becomes a break.

chapters.title: The Shift Change
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The plan: cross at Checkpoint Nine during the 04:00 shift change, when the compromised guards rotate out. Lena, too hurt to travel, insists on releasing the archive regardless — a deadline neither can control. Emotional beat: ticking clock, tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: Interception at Kilometer Forty
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The second team ambushes the road short of the checkpoint. Mara arrives off-book and turns the fight, taking a bullet shielding Rafael. Emotional beat: violence rendered intimate; the choice made flesh.

chapters.title: The Border
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Carrying Mara, he crosses during the shift change as the checkpoint lights die behind them — the governments have burned the crossing to erase the corridor. Emotional beat: exhaustion, grief for Lena's sacrifice, and the strange peace of having nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Press Room Gambit
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. From neutral territory, Lena's archive goes live simultaneously in three countries; Rafael hands the chips to an international safety board, not the police. Emotional beat: the pivot from fugitive to witness — power reclaimed by testimony.

chapters.title: The Director's Fall
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The aviation director tries to flee via private charter; the charter is grounded by the very regulators he corrupted. His ministers resign in sequence. Emotional beat: power devouring itself; justice arriving unglamorous and procedural.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Rafael and Mara's shared POV. Mara, recovering, testifies about the stand-down order; Rafael describes row twelve without breaking. Emotional beat: grief spoken aloud finally becomes bearable; belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The House That Sold Itself
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He returns to the safe house one last time, now legally his to sell, and takes down the evidence wall — leaving only the photograph from row twelve's memorial. Emotional beat: closing the wound without pretending it never happened.

chapters.title: Go-Bag, Unpacked
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating Rafael and Mara. Months later, Rafael unpacks the go-bag into drawers — a life with an address. Mara plants tomatoes badly in the garden by the memorial wall. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; survival transformed into living, love chosen over duty at last.
